questions: When the board is fully visible, does it hold exactly three pens arranged in a single row?
Are all three pens aligned identically, all pointing the same way, including any pen near the left or right frame edge as it enters or exits?
Do all three pens share identical barrel and cap colors, with no mismatch?
Is every pen fully capped with no exposed writing tip, and are all three pens equal in length?
Does the board advance steadily from left to right at EVERY moment, never halting, freezing, or pausing even briefly (1-3 seconds) at any point in the video?
Do all pens stay fixed in their positions on the board, with no pen shifting, sliding, or moving on its own relative to the board mid-clip?

question_answers.evidence: In frames 7 through 12, the board is fully visible and carries exactly three pens arranged in a row.

The pens are not aligned identically. In frames 8-12, the rightmost pen has its cap at the top, the middle pen has its cap at the bottom, and the leftmost pen appears to have its writing tip exposed at the bottom.
All three pens appear to have translucent barrels and black components (caps or tips), so they share the same general color scheme, although their orientation/state differs.

The leftmost pen (visible clearly in frames 8-12) shows a dark, pointed writing tip at the bottom, indicating it is uncapped, while the others are capped. Also, the middle pen is capped at the bottom, unlike the right pen capped at the top.
The board moves steadily from left to right across the sequence of frames without stopping or reversing.
The pens remain fixed in their relative positions on the board throughout the movement.

parsed.reason: The video shows multiple anomalies: the pens are not oriented in the same direction (one cap up, one cap down), and the leftmost pen appears to be missing its cap, exposing the writing tip.

description: One pen is flipped and a pen is missing its cap (combined anomaly).
